newsitem.title: USA: U.S wholesale prices decline 0.4 percent in February.
newsitem.headline: U.S wholesale prices decline 0.4 percent in February.

text.p: Prices at the wholesale level tumbled in February, the Labor Department said on Friday, the latest indication that inflationay pressures have been largely wrung out of the economy.
The department said the Producer Price Index fell 0.4 percent after declining 0.3 percent in January. It was the first time since the autumn of 1994 that the index retreated two months in a row.

Excluding the often-volatile food and energy sector, the so-called core rate that economists believe more closely tracks inflation, also declined, falling 0.1 percent in February after being unchanged in January.
The report was far better than Wall Street estimates, which saw overall wholesale prices falling 0.1 percent and the core rate edging up 0.1 percent.
The department said energy prices fell 1.2 percent in February after a decline of 0.2 percent in the prior month.
Gasoline prices retreated 3.1 percent after jumping 2.6 percent, while home heating oil was off 1.1 percent after falling 2.8 percent in January.
Food prices also fell, dropping 0.3 percent after moving lower by 1.0 percent in January, as meat and fish costs turned lower.
The department also noted that computer prices in February fell a record 5.2 percent, eclipsing the previous record fall of 4.0 percent in July 1991.
Auto prices, which fell 0.4 percent in January, rose 0.2 percent in Feburary, the department said.
Goods at the intermediate level of production that require additional processing fell 0.1 percent after being up 0.2 percent in January.
Prices at the early part of the production cycle, so-called crude goods, fell 5.9 percent in February after rising 5.2 percent in the prior month.
Wholesale prices fell 0.2 percent in September 1994 and 0.4 percent in October of that year.
